title: Tools and function invocation
summary: Tools are functions the model can request. The framework runs the tool loop: model asks, framework calls the function, result goes back, until the model answers or a limit stops it.
useIf: The agent must read data, call APIs or act, and you want the framework to run the call loop with limits and middleware.
avoidIf: The call is deterministic and always needed: call it in code and pass the result in as context.

explain.md: **Function tools** are your code with a schema. In Python pass any function (docstring becomes the description, `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)]` documents parameters) or decorate it with `@tool`. In .NET use `AIFunctionFactory.Create(method)` [[tr5]]. **Other tool sources**: MCP servers the agent process connects to (`MCPStreamableHTTPTool`, `MCPStdioTool`), hosted tools that the provider runs (web search, code interpreter, hosted MCP via client `get_*_tool()` methods) and other agents wrapped as tools [[tr36]].

**The loop.** In Python the `FunctionInvocation` layer in the chat client runs the loop. Several tool calls in one assistant message run concurrently by default; set `allow_concurrent_invocation` to `False` when tools share mutable state. `max_function_calls` and `max_duration_seconds` default to `None` (unlimited) and are best-effort: they are checked after each model-requested batch, so a batch can overshoot. Time waiting for tool approval counts toward the duration limit [[tr5]].

**Errors are filtered.** `include_detailed_errors` defaults to `False`, so the model gets a generic failure and the original exception stays available to trusted host code. Turn it on only when the result stays on a trusted channel [[tr5]]. On a Harness Agent function invocation is wired for you, and `@tool` functions default to `approval_mode="never_require"` [[tr5]].

steps.title: Model call
steps.md: Chat middleware runs, the model returns text or tool calls.

steps.title: Approval check
steps.md: Tools marked for approval pause the run and return a request.

steps.title: Tool calls
steps.md: Function middleware wraps each call; calls in one message run concurrently by default.

steps.title: Limits
steps.md: Stop at `max_iterations`, `max_function_calls` or `max_duration_seconds`, then ask for a final text answer.

whereToUse: Read-only lookups: order status, knowledge search, calendar free/busy
Actions with side effects, gated by approval (see tool approval)
MCP servers that expose a shared tool catalogue across agents
Provider-hosted tools such as web search or code interpreter when the client supports them
Agents wrapped as tools so a primary agent keeps ownership of the task

use: The model must choose among actions at run time
The tool has a stable, well-described schema and bounded cost
You want middleware, telemetry and approval to apply per call
avoid: The call always happens: do it in code, fewer tokens and no variance
The tool returns huge payloads: shrink or summarise before returning, since results are re-sent to the model
The tool needs a secret the model could see: keep secrets in the host and inject runtime-only values
flips: Tools share mutable state: set `allow_concurrent_invocation` to `False` so calls run in model order
A hosted MCP tool must be traced end to end: use a client-opened MCP transport, because provider-issued calls get no `_meta` trace context

pitfalls.symptom: A run loops through tools for minutes and costs spike
pitfalls.cause: No call or time cap: `max_function_calls` and `max_duration_seconds` default to unlimited
pitfalls.fix: Set explicit limits and watch `gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_calls` in telemetry [[tr5]]

pitfalls.cause: Calls in one assistant message run concurrently by default
pitfalls.fix: Set `allow_concurrent_invocation=False` or make tools safe to run in parallel

pitfalls.symptom: Debugging shows only a generic tool failure
pitfalls.cause: `include_detailed_errors` is `False`, so the model sees a generic result
pitfalls.fix: Read `Content.exception` in trusted host code or logs; enable detailed errors only for trusted channels

scenarios.title: Shared tool catalogue for several agents
scenarios.situation: Five teams want the same 20 internal tools. A platform team owns them. Agents run in different services. Security requires traces that cross into the tool server.
constraints: Shared catalogue owned by one team
Agents run in the team's own process
unknowns: Is the MCP server on the private network?
Who authenticates the agent to the server?
How big is the tool list in tokens?
scenarios.question: How do agents consume the tools?

options.name: A client-opened MCP connection from each agent process
options.why: The framework injects W3C trace context into `params._meta` for sessions the agent process opens, so traces cross into the server.
options.tradeoff: Each agent holds a connection and must handle auth and a large tool list.

options.name: Provider-hosted MCP tool configuration
options.why: Little code and the provider manages the connection.
options.tradeoff: The provider issues `tools/call`, so no `_meta` trace context is injected and the chain breaks.

options.name: Copy the 20 functions into each team's code
options.why: Divergent copies and no central ownership.
options.tradeoff: Only sensible for two or three tiny tools nobody else needs.

flips.if: Tracing across the boundary is not required and the provider supports hosted MCP
flips.then: The hosted connector becomes attractive for simplicity.

flips.if: The tool list is very large
flips.then: Add progressive tool exposure from a context provider.

scenarios.takeaway: Who opens the MCP session decides who can propagate trace context.

scenarios.title: Stop a runaway tool loop
scenarios.situation: A research agent sometimes calls a search tool 40 times for one question. Each call returns 8 KB. Latency target is 20 seconds.
unknowns: Is the model re-searching because results are poor?
Is partial output acceptable at the limit?
scenarios.question: What do you change first?

options.name: Set `max_function_calls` and `max_duration_seconds`, and shrink tool results with a result parser
options.why: Limits bound the loop and a smaller result cuts tokens per iteration. At a limit the client asks for a final text answer.
options.tradeoff: Limits are best-effort and a batch can overshoot.

options.name: Raise `max_iterations` to be safe
options.why: It lengthens the loop and cost.
options.tradeoff: Only right when answers truly need many steps and budget allows.

options.name: Disable the tool
options.tradeoff: Loses the capability the agent exists for.

flips.if: The task really needs long searches
flips.then: Move to a Harness Agent with compaction and background execution.

flips.if: Results are poor and the model keeps re-searching
flips.then: Fix retrieval quality or the tool description first; limits only hide the symptom.

scenarios.takeaway: Cap the loop and slim the payload before you tune the prompt.

quiz.q: Your agent opened an MCP session with `MCPStreamableHTTPTool` and traces reach the server. After you switch to a provider-hosted MCP configuration the server spans are orphaned. Why?
options: The provider runtime issues `tools/call`, so the framework cannot inject `params._meta` context
quiz.explain: The framework injects trace context only for MCP sessions the agent process itself opens. Hosted connectors are called by the provider.

quiz.q: Which statements about Python tool limits are true? Select all.
options: Limits are checked after each model-requested batch, so a batch can exceed them
Time waiting for approval counts toward `max_duration_seconds`
At a limit the client raises an exception to the caller
quiz.explain: The docs say the client stops invoking tools and asks the model for a final text response, not an exception. The first three are stated as written.
